references.text: The Lord commands that every firstborn that opens the womb shall be consecrated to him, both of humans and animals.
The law concerning giving to the Lord everything that opens the womb, including the firstborn of cattle and sheep.
The commandment to give the firstborn of sons and of cattle and sheep to the Lord.
Continuation of the same legal text regarding the redemption of the firstborn donkey and sons.
The Lord declares that all firstborn belong to him from the day he struck down the firstborn in Egypt.
Rules concerning the redemption of firstborn humans and unclean animals, as well as the offering of the firstborn of cattle, sheep, and goats.
Every male firstborn of cattle and sheep shall be consecrated to the Lord.
Nehemiah renews the covenant to bring the firstborn of sons and livestock to the house of the Lord.
Luke cites the law that every male firstborn that opens the womb is to be called holy to the Lord.
Complementary legal provision: Exodus establishes the requirement for consecration, while Numbers specifies the redemption rule for unclean animals and humans.
Parallel legislation: Both verses establish the same fundamental requirement that the firstborn males belong to the Lord.
Consequence of consecration: Both verses emphasize that firstborn animals must not be used for ordinary work or production.
Theological parallel: 22:28 confirms the principle in 34:19 by applying it to human firstborns.
Ritual elaboration: 22:29 specifies the timeframe (the eighth day) for fulfilling the requirement in 34:19.
